quest.title: The Child Who Doesn't Exist
quest.description: It's a fine day. Yes, a fine day for a stroll around Poisson!
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon knows that voice...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Over here!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: To borrow one of the more popular turns of phrase at the moment, this appears to be quite the "fated reunion." Running into you two out of the blue like this has really made my day. I certainly wasn't expecting it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can say that again! What brings you to Poisson?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Paimon's got it! You must be here for one of your magic shows, right?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Um... Actually, we've run into a bit of trouble on the home front, so "Father" arranged for us to stay in Poisson for the time being.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, are Lynette and Freminet here too?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Yep, along with most of the other members of the House of the Hearth. You may have noticed Poisson seems a bit more... crowded than usual.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you're saying nearly the entire organization has moved to Poisson? Sounds like you've run into way more than just "a bit of trouble." What's really going on?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Umm... Well...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Since the two of you are so curious, perhaps I can fill in the gaps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ack! You scared Paimon half to death!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: "Father," you're here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Y'know? On second thought, maybe we don't need to know. It's all probably super confidential House of the Hearth stuff, right? We totally weren't trying to pry or anything...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: No need to be nervous. I could sense your genuine concern from your conversation just now.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Of course, I can also understand your confusion. Sending so many Fatui here to Poisson, it's only natural that some might suspect an "ulterior motive" to be involved.

choices.text: Well, we are a little curious...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I understand. I'm well aware you've had your fair share of confrontations with the Fatui in the past. And I can't exactly guarantee that we'll remain on good terms in the future.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As for right now, however, I would say we have little reason to be at odds, wouldn't you agree? The House of the Hearth could stand to be more open with those who have worked so closely with us in the past.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As for the issue at hand... Well, it hardly relates to any ulterior motive. To be frank, it all stems from a certain rumor circulating around the House of the Hearth. It's an internal matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What sort of rumor?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: A rumor that a certain "phantom child" is hiding away in the House of the Hearth.

choices.text: Some sort of ghost story, maybe?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A phantom child? Just hearing the name is giving Paimon the creeps...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: A spirit that should have long ceased to exist is lurking in the shadows of the House of the Hearth.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: So, I decided to bring the children to Poisson before continuing to investigate the situation. I expect I should be able to track down the spirit fairly quickly. After that, it's just a matter of "resolving" the situation, if you will. It shouldn't be much trouble at all.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: If you're curious, or if you still have some concerns, it might be advisable to stick around for a few days. I'm sure the children would be exceedingly pleased to welcome some visitors.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Lyney, I'll leave you to entertain our guests. I have some matters to attend to.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course, "Father."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I couldn't help but feel intimidated during that conversation with The Knave. Now that she's gone, it feels like I can finally breathe again...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She also suggested that we stick around for a few days... But why?)

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm, it has long been a dream of mine to invite you to our home, and introduce you to my other siblings.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You're quite well-known in the organization already. A lot of people have been talking about you, especially after everything with the prophecy.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If you're willing, why don't you stay awhile and have a little chat with us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, alright! We don't have anything else to do right now anyway. But let's be clear, we're just gonna be there as guests, okay? Don't get any funny... Wait a second! If we're your "guests," that probably means we'll be treated to lots of yummy food, right?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course! During our stay in Poisson, we've been helping out the locals with some fishing. We bring in quite the bounty every day. In fact, today is the perfect chance for me to show you what I can do in the kitchen.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Let's go. I'll take you to where we're staying.

choices.text: I feel like I'm getting chills already.
We still have our reservations about your organization.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We rented this house from one of the locals to use as a temporary base. I'll come back later and tidy up a bit. After that, it should be all ready for you to stay in tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome, thanks! So where are we off to now?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, when I happened to run into you two earlier, I was actually in the middle of distributing some supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: With this many people staying in Poisson, we have to bring in outside supplies every now and then. I should probably make sure the rest of these provisions get delivered, otherwise people might start to get antsy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! We'll come with!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are all sorts of rumors about your organization floating around out there. Paimon's not sure she could even take a wild guess as to what's true and what's not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, now that we finally have the chance to see a day in the life of the House, we can take a good look at how you operate.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, you're more than welcome to come along. Just follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: Lyney! You're finally here! The supplies... I'm assuming you've—

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Brought them with me? Yep, here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Uh... hello? Something caught your eye?

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: #It's {NICKNAME} and Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: No way!

dialogues.speaker: Heloir
dialogues.text: #C'mere everyone! Hurry! {NICKNAME} and Paimon are here!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: One at a time please. Don't crowd around them all at once. We don't want to scare off our guests, now do we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's alright. Gotta say, Paimon didn't realize we were THIS famous...

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: Of course! "Father" and Lyney have told us so much about you!

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: "Father" told us about how you helped Lyney. According to her, you're a trustworthy friend, and as far as she's concerned, that's pretty much the highest compliment we've ever heard her give. As you can imagine, everyone's been very curious about you.

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: #I heard {NICKNAME} is so strong that {M#he}{F#she} can move a mountain with {M#his}{F#her} bare hands!

dialogues.speaker: Heloir
dialogues.text: I heard Paimon eats so much that she can clean out the entire pantry at Hotel Debord in just three days!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a second, that's the rumor you've heard about Paimon!? Not cool at all!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mine's also a bit of a stretch...

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: Oh, wait! When guests visit, you're supposed to give them gifts and stuff, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we don't need something like that. Besides, we don't have anything to give to you...

dialogues.speaker: Heloir
dialogues.text: C'mon, we insist! I can give you some of my new potions? Just pick your poison — and by that I mean medicine or actual poison. I've got both.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: Ooor, maybe Chapleau can teach you guys about stealth! He's super good at it! He's never been caught!

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: Ah, now that's not a bad idea! I know you usually prefer to fight head-on, but it never hurts to expand your bag of tricks, right? When it comes to eliminating your enemies, staying quiet can go a long way. Trust me — I would know.

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: I was poisoned not too long ago, and I'm still dealing with the aftereffects, so I'm not quite as good as I was before... but I can still give you some pointers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, wait, uh... When you said gifts, Paimon didn't think you meant poison and stealth tactics!

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: But those are the best things we can give you! You don't like them?

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: Ooh! How about this? Tell me the name of someone who really annoys you, and we'll teach 'em a lesson for you!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The dangerous suggestions keep on coming one after another. You start to get a bit overwhelmed...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Alright, Foltz, Heloir — I think that's enough suggestions for now. When it comes to being a good host, it's the thought that counts.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You don't need a physical gift to make our guests happy. In fact, pestering them with suggestion after suggestion might make them more annoyed than anything. I would say your enthusiasm has certainly gotten across.

dialogues.speaker: Heloir
dialogues.text: Really?

response.speaker: Foltz
response.text: Awesome! It's been so long since we've had guests to play with! If there's anything you need, just let us know!

response.speaker: Heloir
response.text: Yeah! Especially if it's poison or something. I've got all sorts of potions for that.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: *ahem* Well, we'll talk to you all later. We've still got supplies to distribute.

response.speaker: Chapleau
response.text: Alright. See you later.

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Bye!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Lyney, about all that poison and stealth tactics talk just now...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Scared you, did it? That kind of talk comes with being part of the House of the Hearth.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: When Foltz was really young, he strangled all of his family pets — just out of curiosity. He was labeled a dangerous "problem child" and was abandoned by his family.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Heloir has an unnatural obsession with potions. "Father" has forbidden her from trying all the different concoctions she comes up with, but she still tries to test them in secret. You really have to keep an eye on that one.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Chapleau is around my age. While I'm mainly responsible for collecting intelligence, he handles surveillance. He's very passionate about his work and has no reservations about taking on some very difficult missions.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I know you two probably aren't used to that kind of talk, but I can promise you they only had the best of intentions. Things like stealth tactics and developing different poisons... they really mean a lot to them. They were just trying to share the best of what they could offer — that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Filliol, supplies are here.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: Thanks. And who are these two? Outsiders?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #Ah, allow me to introduce you. This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: Oh, you're the famous duo I've been hearing so much about.

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: It's nice to meet you. I heard you've traveled to all sorts of places. Is that true?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! We're making our way all across Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: Oh, good for you.

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: You must be pretty familiar with Fontaine by now, then. Have you seen the new opera that started running recently? I think it's called... "The Four Thousand Thieves"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the first we've heard of it!

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: It seems like it's going to be fantastic — from what I've been able to tell from the posters, anyway. You should definitely check it out if you have the time.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: Oh, and there's "The Blind Maiden" too. That one is supposed to have audience interaction. Seems pretty interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you spend some time talking about popular culture, the atmosphere becomes more and more relaxed...

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: After this mission is over, I think I'll go get a manicure.

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: Maybe I should dye my hair. Hmm, wonder how much it'll cost...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it just Paimon, or do these two seem much easier to get along with than the others... Looks like the House of the Hearth has some "normal" members, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: I heard that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Uh... Oops, hehe...

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: I'm guessing you're referring to Foltz and the others? Yeah, we're definitely not all like them.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: I bet those crazies are practically foaming at the mouth right now. Heh, I'm sure they just can't wait to get back to Snezhnaya to carry out the plan...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That's enough, Filliol.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: Ah, "don't talk about family members behind their back," right? Heh, whatever. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: Um, guess this is goodbye then! If you ever have some time, we should go see the opera together!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, that's it for the supplies. We should probably head back as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they didn't seem too happy with each other. Seems like there could be something more going on here...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right. We're only here as "guests," after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Lyney's getting super far ahead! C'mon, let's catch up!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So... What do you think of the members you've met so far?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They've certainly got a lot of personality.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Haha, well, "Father" is always encouraging us to be strong-willed and independent. So, if there's one thing we've got, it's people who aren't afraid to speak their mind.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, I should probably get cooking. Wanna join?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Then let's head out... Huh? Freminet? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Ah, well, um...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Freminet! Nice to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: You too. I heard you're here as guests of the House of the Hearth. Welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: #We were just going to make some food. Why don't you come along? I could use some help in the kitchen, and I seem to remember you mentioning you wanted to make Seafood Soup for {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seafood Soup! Paimon's drooling already!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Were you looking for something just now, Freminet? Maybe I can help.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Ah, it's nothing. I just wanted to see if there were any extra supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Yeah, we've got some left over. What do you need?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Some food and water. And some clean cloth, if possible.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No problem. Give me a second here. Food, water...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Wait a minute... What do you need all of those for? You're not on any missions, as far as I'm aware, and you were just going to come eat with us... So what's this all about?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I—I thought I'd grab an extra portion because I get hungry at night. Could be because I'm growing, y'know, and...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Freminet.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You remember what I told you? You're not like me — your lying skills still need some work.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Tell me what's going on. Is it really bad enough that you have to keep it from your own brother?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Maybe it'll be better if we gave them some space...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Huh, this is the first time I've seen that kind of look on your face. Whatever happened... Does it have something to do with "Father"?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Just... follow me.

talks.objective: Figure out what Freminet is hiding

dialogues.text: You're back! Oh, and you've brought some friends with you this time!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hello, my name's Lyney. I grew up in the House of the Hearth. And you are...
Hi, Lyney. I'm also a child of the House of the Hearth — just like you!

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: You can call me Clervie.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Clervie?

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: It's nice to meet you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that name ring any bells, Lyney?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: No, not at all. That's not a name we have on our roster — I'm sure of it. What I'm not sure of, though... is how she managed to sneak in.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: She must be the "phantom child" "Father" has been searching for. From the looks of it, I'm guessing you were the one that found her, Freminet? You, uh... haven't told "Father," have you?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: No, I haven't told anyone. I've just been... keeping her hidden.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: For how long?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: About half a month now.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So, ever since we got to Poisson, then? Do you have any idea what you're doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I know what I'm doing.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Really? 'Cause from where I'm standing, it looks like you're hiding the very person "Father" has been trying to find! If "Father" finds out about this, everyone involved is going to be punished.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You know the rules of the House, Freminet. I know you do — "Father" doesn't tolerate any form of betrayal. So, why are you doing this?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I've thought it through... And I just can't hand her over like that.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Lyney, don't you remember last year? Chapleau nearly died after getting poisoned during that one mission. He wasn't able to get back before the poison started taking effect, and not a single person was there to help him.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: That night, while I was sleeping, I heard a voice telling me to go save him. I opened my eyes, but I couldn't find the source of the voice. I thought maybe I was just hearing things, but I went to look for him anyway. Luckily, I got there with enough time to save his life.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: That feeling of being "haunted," of hearing voices... It's happened many times in the House of the Hearth. I'm sure you've noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So what you're saying is... That was her? She was the one who spoke to you that night?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Unless there are other spirits roaming around the House of the Hearth, I don't think there's any other possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: If Clervie were our enemy, it wouldn't matter whether she was a spirit or an actual child — I would have acted without a second thought, because that's what "Father" ordered us to do.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: But, she's been living with us, helping us from the shadows all this time. I think that makes her family.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I couldn't just hand her over to be dealt with — not when there's so much we still don't know.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: So what's your plan then? You can't keep her here forever. Someone is bound to find out eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I haven't thought that far yet. I don't want to disobey an order from "Father," but I also don't want to put Clervie in danger.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Come with me. There are a couple things I'd like to say to you in private.

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: Those two sure care a lot about each other.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, they got a funny way of showing it. From where Paimon was floating, it sure seemed like they were about to bite each other's heads off...

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: No way! They have a really deep bond. I could tell right away, 'cause I also have a friend like that.

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: I just... don't know how long that kind of bond can last.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: The darkness in the House runs deeper than you can imagine. No one can get out alive.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Lyney. I really didn't mean to drag anyone else into this...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh, really? You didn't mean to? 'Cause I, for one, wish you did.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Y'know, when we were younger, you didn't call me "Lyney." You called me "Brother," just like Lynette.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: We grew up together, the three of us. We were all orphans, all rescued by "Father." Of all the siblings in the House of the Hearth, I think our bond was the closest.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Later on, when you started calling me "Lyney," I wasn't actually surprised. After all, Lynette and I are related by blood. We've had to depend on each other to survive long before we joined the House.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Lyney, I...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: The darkest and most difficult moments of my life happened before you and I had ever met — I'm sure that's true for you as well. Even so, Freminet, we've stood by each other for all these years now, and, to me, that means more than blood.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: You and Lynette are the most important people in my life. No one can replace you. So, I won't let you face anything alone — not if I can help it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, looks like things are getting kinda heated between Lyney and Freminet... Maybe we should go check on them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, you two... Hope we aren't interrupting anything, like a fight or...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute! Freminet! Y—You're not... crying, are you? Is everything alright?

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: Everything's fine... Thanks for asking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we're all friends here, right? We've been through so much together, so if there's anything we can do to help, just say the word!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It's just a small family dispute. It's not something our guests should trouble themselves with. In fact, it might be better if your stay ended here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But sometimes, having guests around can come in handy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... What are you getting at, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: When guests are around, families are often on their best behavior... and any disputes are less likely to escalate... That's what you're trying to say, isn't it?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I... just... Thank you. I was really hoping to keep you out of it, but even if I could think of some other reason to turn you away, I'm not sure I could convince you. I know things could turn dangerous, so I promise you this — from now on, I'll protect you like my life depends on it.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Me too.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, back to the matter at hand, then. If we don't plan on handing Clervie over to "Father," then our only other option is to solve the mystery of her identity before "Father" is able to track her down.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: That means finding out where she came from and what she's doing here. Then, we can send her on her merry way and pretend like none of this ever happened.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: I've tried that already.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And?

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: And... nothing. I tried taking her somewhere really far away, but... after some time, she just reappeared.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: She even came with us all the way to Poisson. It seems like wherever the House is, she follows.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm, I don't know much about spirits... Do you two have any ideas?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see here... Ooh! Paimon remembers hearing something like... If you fulfill a spirit's last wish before they died, they'll let go of whatever's keeping them here and return to the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just that... Paimon doesn't really remember where she heard that... so it's not guaranteed to work or anything.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, sounds like it's worth a shot. Guess that means we should go ask her about her wish. But first... Freminet, I need you to promise me something.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: What is it?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I need you to promise me that this will stay between the two of us. We're the masterminds behind this whole thing — no one else gets involved. Can you do that for me?

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Of course. I promise.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Alright, then let's seal the promise just like when we were kids... Fist bump on three. Ready? One, two, three...

response.speaker: Lyney & Freminet & Lynette
response.text: I swear.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Ah!!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Whoa!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: L—Lynette!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You scared me!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Wh—What a surprise! *ahem* What brings you here, dear sister?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And, uh... When exactly did you get here?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: You're an idiot, Brother.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Um...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: And you too, Freminet.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: #You three, {NICKNAME}. And you four, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what did we do?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I've seen Clervie around the House of the Hearth before. I hadn't seen her in Poisson, so I figured she must not have come with us... But it turns out you were just hiding her.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: I heard you talking about your plan. Rather than steering clear of the situation, I'd rather fully join in.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: If you don't agree, I'll have no choice but to report everything back to "Father." Simple as that.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: *sigh* You're not giving us much wiggle room here, Lynette.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, I guess we're all in this together, then. After we talk to Clervie, we'll figure out our next move.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: There's no time to lose. Let's go.

choices.text: I think it'll be better if we stick around.

dialogues.speaker: Clervie
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm full! Thank you for bringing me this food, you guys.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said she's "full," but the food doesn't look like it's even been touched...

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: That's right. Based on what I've been able to observe, it doesn't seem like Clervie can interact with the physical world at all.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Still, when she's presented with food, she'll always linger around it for a good little while. Maybe, in her mind, she really is eating those things.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Does she know that she has already passed away?

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: I've tried to ask her, but she didn't answer. My guess is that she's just as confused as we are, or... Maybe she couldn't understand the question at all.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Clervie, if you've got some time, I'd like to ask you a few questions.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Oh! Another new friend! Hi, I'm Clervie.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Hello.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Clervie, how did you join the House of the Hearth?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Huh? Isn't it the same for everybody?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: The Knave brings you here, and then you can't leave.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It's just that... your name, it's not on the roster. And I've never seen you before.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: The roster? Ah, I get it now. I think there might be some things you don't know about this place.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: The people in charge... They're not as nice as they look. They say they keep a roster... but it's not complete. There are a lot of people who aren't on it... and never will be.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: In this House, some people are "family" and other people... are just "test subjects." Those kinds of people aren't ever going to get a place on the roster... unless it's the roster of people who've been executed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, does that mean The Knave, she...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Is there anyone that can vouch for you?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Perrie. She's my best friend. She's the only one I trust in this place.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Have either of you heard of that name before?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: No.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: Me neither...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Clervie... Perrie... Neither of those names are on the roster.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But... it seems like she's telling the truth. Either that, or this kid's already got a bag of tricks bigger than mine.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hmm, maybe we should try a different approach. Clervie, do you have a wish?

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: A wish?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It can be anything you want. Just imagine — it's your birthday, you're blowing out the candles, and your wish is...

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: To... To go outside.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: Where the sun can find me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's it? Well, that sounds easy enough.

response.speaker: Clervie
response.text: The darkness in the House runs deeper than you can imagine. No one can get out alive.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (What did she mean by that...? Things can't be this simple.)

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Okay, time to divide and conquer. Listen up. I've got a plan.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'll try and find a way to use basic illusory magic to take Clervie outside and bring her somewhere with sunlight.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Lynette, try and find the list of executions that Clervie was talking about, and see if her name is on it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Freminet, you stay in Poisson. We can't be the only ones who've had run ins with Clervie. I need you to collect intel on everything she's said and done.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Freminet
response.text: I'll try my best.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about us? What should we do?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I really appreciate your willingness to help, but this is a family matter. I don't want to drag you in too deep. It's too risky.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Let me think... Since "Father" considers you to be guests, maybe you could stick by her side for a little while? You don't need to do anything except keep up some nice, casual conversation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon gets it! You want us to distract her!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How should we contact you?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'll give you a magic bird. If "Father" suspects something, all you need to do is release it when she's not looking, and it'll alert me that something's wrong.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course, that's only as a last resort. If "Father" doesn't seem to notice us, there's no need to make contact. We'll reconvene here tonight after all's said and done.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: If the worst-case scenario happens, and we're discovered, just tell "Father" everything. We're not going to let our guests get punished for our own actions — that's where we draw the line.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be careful.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You too... Okay, this is where we part. "Father" should be at the beach nearby.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I really hope this goes well. No... It has to go well. That's the only way this can get resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Chapleau
dialogues.text: #Wow, {NICKNAME} and Paimon... I finally got to meet them in person!

dialogues.speaker: Heloir
dialogues.text: Hmm, they don't really seem as intimidating as you hear in the stories.

dialogues.speaker: Foltz
dialogues.text: They'd probably get along really well with Filliol... If only they got here sooner.

dialogues.speaker: Filliol
dialogues.text: Looks like there's more trouble in store next month too... *sigh* When will it end...

dialogues.speaker: Nanteuil
dialogues.text: Hey, just focus on the positives. At least our time in Poisson has been pretty relaxing. Don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's been a while since we visited Poisson. Maybe we should head over and have a look around?
